To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
histone deacetylation activity is required to repress E2F‐mediated apoptosis in mature neurones.
the histone deacetylation machinery is required for the maintenance of neuronal homeostasis and that its deregulation leads to neuronal cell death.
histone deacetylation controls the transcriptional response of neuronal cells to apoptotic stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the transcription of E‐2F genes, which play a crucial role in the control of the cell cycle and in the induction of apoptosis.
the role of chromatin in the control of neuronal fate.
the mechanisms of neuronal death and, in particular, with those of apoptosis, which is a genetically programmed form of death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
histone deacetylation is a key factor in the regulation of E2F activity, which plays a critical role in neuronal cell fate.
the inhibition of histone deactylase activity in mature neurons induces an E2F dependent transcription of genes involved in apoptosis.
histone deacetylation is required for neuronal survival, and histone acetylations, for apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

histone acetylases and deacetylases are involved in the regulation of neuronal apoptosis, and that histone deacetylation plays a role in the repression of the E2F‐target gene e2f‐ 1 in mature neurones.

histone deacetylation is required for the repression of the e 2 f‐1 gene in neuronal cells, and that the inhibition of histone deacytlases leads to a derepression of the e2 f‐1 and other E2F‐controlled genes that are required for apoptosis.
histone deacetylation activity in mature neurones is necessary to maintain the survival programme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
histone deacetylation may be involved in the regulation of neuronal apoptosis through a mechanism that relies on the E2F transcription factors.
histone acetylations are not only important for transcriptional activation but also for repression.
histone acetylations are not the sole determinant in the regulation of E2F activity.
